title: About The World of AI

sections.body:
The World of AI is a reference atlas for artificial intelligence: what the law says, who is suing whom, and what the words mean. It tracks AI legislation in all fifty states and the District of Columbia, maintains living pages for active AI lawsuits in United States courts, and publishes a working glossary of the vocabulary the field actually uses.

It is a reference site, not a news blog. Pages are built to be read once and cited later.

The World of AI is published by SRJ Consulting & Services LLC, a Texas company founded by Stephen R. Jordan that advises organizations on AI governance and publishes a book series on the subject at srjconsultingservices.com. The consulting practice pays for this site; the site does not sell consulting to read it.

Every fact on this site traces to a public source. Legislation comes from LegiScan, which aggregates state legislature records. Litigation comes from CourtListener and the federal dockets it mirrors. Federal regulatory activity comes from the Federal Register. Research comes from arXiv. Definitions and explanatory material are written and maintained by SRJ. Each page links its sources so you can check our work.

An automated pipeline refreshes the underlying database every day and rebuilds the site from it. Nothing is typed into a page by hand at publication time, which is why every page carries a last-verified date that means something. When a source updates, the page updates on the next run.

Four rules govern everything here. We do not invent facts: where data is missing, the page says less. We correct known errors immediately at the source rather than deferring them. We label everything paid, and no commercial relationship changes a verdict or a legal status. And we write in plain English, because a reference that needs translating is not a reference.
Quote us, link to us, and build on our public API at /api/. Attribution and a link are all we ask. Details are in our Terms of Use.
If something here is wrong, tell us and we will fix it: info@srjconsultingservices.com. Corrections are the fastest way to improve this site and we treat them as a favor, not a complaint.
